{{< pagebreak >}}

Construction of epidemics
=========================
Parameters: initial state and duration
--------------------------------------
We shall only use artificial examples,
so the rate parameters need not be defined.
```{julia}
const duration = 5.0 ; const initial  = SIR(0.0, 4, 1, 0) ;
```

Construction of unconditioned epidemic
--------------------------------------
Here is an `Innovation` to generate the `Evolution` of the unconditioned epidemic:
```{julia}
AI = AbstractInfection; I = Infection; P = PInfection; NF  = NoFlyInfection; XI = ExpungedInfection;
AR = AbstractRemoval;   R = Removal;   C = CRemoval;   KI = KilledInfection; KR = KilledRemoval;

infections = I[I(2t-1, t, t+1) for t ∈ [1,2]] ∪ AI[I(0,3,4), I(2,4,5)]
uremovals  = R[R(2t, t) for t ∈ [1,2]] ∪ [R(1,5), R(3,5), R(4,5)]

uiv1 = Innovation(initial.n, infections, uremovals)
```
The corresponding `Evolution` of an (_unconditioned_) epidemic is given as follows:
```{julia}
uev1 = Evolution(initial, uiv1)
```

{{< pagebreak >}}

Construction of conditioned epidemic
------------------------------------
Here is an `Innovation` to generate the `CEvolution` of the corresponding conditioned epidemic:
```{julia}
removals   = R[R(1,5), R(3,5), R(4,5)]
cremovals  = C[C(2t, t) for t ∈ [1,2]] 

iv1 = Innovation(initial.n, infections, removals, cremovals)
```
The `CEvolution` of an epidemic (_conditioned_ on observed removals) is given as follows:
```{julia}
ev1 = CEvolution(initial, iv1)
```
Notice that this `CEvolution` omits crucial information 
(fields `LFE`, `NFZ1`, `NFZ2`, `NFZ3` are empty lists here:
they would generally be filled using information from the `AbstractEvolution`
immediately preceding the `CEvolution` in the sense of algorithmic time).
This particular `CEvolution` then corresponds to the state of the epidemic at step `0` of algorithmic time,
so there is no predecessor evolution in the sense of algorithmic time.

{{< pagebreak >}}

Taking a single step in algorithmic time
========================================

We introduce a new ("candidate")
`Innovation`, which will be used (indirectly) to derive a single step in algorithmic time
of the entire `CEvolution` trajectory.
```{julia} 
infections2c = AI[I(0.75,1,2), I(1.5,1,2), I(0.8,3,4), I(1.5,2,3), I(2.5,1,2), I(3.3,3,4), 
    I(3.6,4,5), I(3.9,4,5), I(4.5,1,3), I(4.4,3,4)] 
removals2c   = R[R(0.5,2), R(2,3), R(1.2,4), R(3.3,1), R(4.5,5), R(4.8,1)]
cremovals2c  = C[C(2, 2), C(4,5)]

iv2c = Innovation(initial.n, infections2c, removals2c, cremovals2c)
```
@fig-test-02-candidate and @fig-test-02-conditioned respectively plot the candidate innovation for step \(1\)
(@fig-test-02-candidate) and a repeat 
from @fig-test-01-conditioned
of the conditional epidemic evolution at step \(0\) (@fig-test-02-conditioned).
```{julia}
#| echo: false
depict("test-02-candidate", new_figure(
    draw_innovation!(deepcopy(lines_plot), iv2c, theme=theme, select=ELEMENTS),
        title="Candidate innovation")
) ;
```


::: {#fig-test-02-innov layout-ncol=2}

`iv2c`
and the conditioned evolution 
`ev1`
of one step previous in algorithmic time.
Direct generation of a `CEvolution` from a candidate innovation such as `iv2c` will typically fail to respect removal-conditioning, so raising an error.

:::



{{< pagebreak >}}

Construction of the next algorithmic step
-----------------------------------------
Here is a function `one_step` which creates a `CEvolution`, namely `ev2_final`,
from an `Evolution` `ev` and an `Innovation` `iv`.
**The code belongs in `EpidemicsCFTP`**!
The procedure is as follows:

1. Test for compatibility between `ev` and `iv`:  
    * Check the `cremoval` lists have the same length;
    * Check the `cremoval` lists generate the same times ('t' field).
2. Use `EpidemicsCFTP.inactive_removals`
to form the new `removals` list by selecting only those `AbstractRemoval`s
from `iv.removals` which will not be activated. Type is changed to
`KilledRemoval` for an `AbstractRemoval` occurring after removal time for the 
corresponding time line. Note that the function discards `Removal`s
(as opposed to `CRemoval`s) which _would_ be activated. 
3. Form the new `cremovals` list using `EpidemicsCFTP.resulting_cremovals`,
by choosing from `iv.cremovals` if activated, otherwise staying with `ev.cremovals`.
4. Compute `LFE`. Note `cremovals` has already been computed in step 3.
Compute `perpetuated_infections` as perpetuations of infections from `LFE` which are original infections.
5. Compute time of last removal per time line (`NFZ1`) and monotonically non-decreasing envelope (`NFZ2`):  
    * select out those `AbstractRemoval`s occurring before actual removal time on each time line;
    * compute `NFZ1`;
    * and generate `NFZ2`.
6. Then generate the next `CEvolution` using the new `removals` and `cremovals` lists,
the new `processed_infections` list, and associated lists
`LFE`, `NFZ1`, `NFZ2` and `NFZ3`.

```{julia}
function one_step(ev::AbstractEvolution, iv::Innovation)::CEvolution
    # Step 1.
    @assert length(ev.cremovals) == length(iv.cremovals)
    @assert all(x.t == y.t for (x,y) ∈ zip(ev.cremovals, iv.cremovals))
    
    # Step 2.
    removals = EpidemicsCFTP.inactive_removals(ev, iv)
    
    # Step 3.
    cremovals  = EpidemicsCFTP.resulting_cremovals(ev, iv.cremovals)
    
    # Step 4.
    duration = maximum(z.t for z in cremovals)
    LFE = EpidemicsCFTP.last_feasible_evolution(duration, ev, 
                iv.infections, cremovals, conditioned=true)
    perpetuated_infections = P[P(z) for z ∈ LFE ∩ ev.infections] 
    
    # Step 5.
    # * Initial computation of `NFZ2`, a **list of times** 
    # indexed by time line ("level"), where each time is initially defined as
    # the supremum of times of **inactivated** `Removal`s at given level or 
    # below. So the envelope increases monotonically with level.
    NFZ1 = repeat([-Inf], ev.initial.n)
    for z ∈ [z for z ∈ removals if z < ev.finis[z.target]]
        NFZ1[z.target] = max(NFZ1[z.target], z.t)
    end
    NFZ2 = accumulate(max, NFZ1)
 
    # The hard work begins! We generate the NFZ3.
    # * The list `processed_infections` of processed `AbstractInfection`s will
    # eventually store (initially in reverse time order) an adjusted version of
    # each infection supplied by the new `Innovation` `iv`.
	processed_infections = AbstractInfection[]
	NFZ3 = deepcopy(NFZ2)
	
	# * Iteration: work backwards through `Infection`s supplied by `iv`
	# together with perpetuated infections,
    # determining in each case how to transform the supplied `Infection`
    # when adding it to the list `processed_infections`.
	for z ∈ reverse(sort(iv.infections ∪ perpetuated_infections))
	    
	    # * If the `Infection` `z` has `target` on the removed portion of a level
        # then it will never be activated, so add `z` as a `KilledInfection`.
	    if (z ≥ ev.finis[z.target])
	        push!(processed_infections, KilledInfection(z))
	        continue
	    end
	    
	    # * If the `Infection` `z` potentially infects a level at a _later time_ 
        # than the current `NFZ2` at that level, then its activation will
        # never break the conditioning (**needs proof!**), so add `z` as-is.
        # (I think the point is: since we are working backwards in time, once
        # `z.t` is considered then `NFZ2` is frozen from time `t` onwards.)
	    #
	    # At this stage of the iteration 
	    @assert(z < ev.finis[z.target])
	    #
        if (z.t ≥ NFZ3[z.infectee])
	        push!(processed_infections, z)
	        continue
	    end
	    
	    # * However if `z.t < NFZ2[z.infectee - 1]` then no issue can arise, as 
        # infection of the level immediately below `z.infectee` will then not be
        # allowed at this time. So again add `z` as-is.
        #
	    # At this stage of the iteration 
	    @assert(z < ev.finis[z.target])
	    @assert(z.t < NFZ3[z.infectee])
	    #
        if (z.t < NFZ3[z.infectee - 1])
	        push!(processed_infections, z)
	        continue
	    end
	    
	    # * Suppose `z ≥ ev.start[z.target]`: then an issue would arise
        # if the level at `z.infectee - 1` were to become infected before `z.t`. 
        #
	    # At this stage of the iteration 
	    @assert(z.t < NFZ3[z.infectee])
	    @assert(z.t ≥ NFZ3[z.infectee - 1])
	    @assert(z < ev.finis[z.target])
	    #
	    # One of two cases must hold:
	    #
	    # * Case (a): Suppose `z < ev.start[z.infectee - 1]`.
        # Then **increase** `NFZ2[z.infectee - 1]` to `z.t` in order to
        # preclude the time line getting infected, and also transform `z` to a
        # `NoFlyInfection` when added to `processed_infections`, to signal
        # that it should never become infected.  
        # Case (b): Alternatively, suppose `z ≥ ev.start[z.infectee - 1]`.
        # Then increasing `NFZ2[z.infectee - 1]` to `z.t` would lead to a
        # problem, since this level is infected at time `z.t`. Therefore we
        # transform `z` to a `ExpungedInfection` when we add it to 
        # `processed_infections`, so that it is treated as an
        # `InoperativeInfection`.
	    if (z ≥ ev.start[z.target])
            if (z < ev.start[z.infectee - 1])
                NFZ3[z.infectee - 1] = z.t
                push!(processed_infections, NoFlyInfection(z))
                # Uncomment for tracking information
                # @info "Conversion of infection into $(NoFlyInfection(z))"
                continue
            else 
                push!(processed_infections, ExpungedInfection(z))
                # Uncomment for tracking information
                # @info "Conversion of infection into $(ExpungedInfection(z))"
                continue 
            end 
	    end
	    
	    # At this stage of the iteration 
	    @assert(z.t < NFZ3[z.infectee])
	    @assert(z.t ≥ NFZ3[z.infectee - 1])
	    @assert(z < ev.start[z.target])
	    # 
	    # * Consider now that potential `Infection`s to be treated later in this
        # iteration must have time mark earlier than `z.t`. If one of these were
        # to infect the level `z.infectee - 1` then it would follow by monotonicity
        # that the `z.target` level would become infected by that time `z.t`; and 
        # thus would create an infection of the `z.infectee` level at time `z.t`. 
        # In order for this to be prevented, we need to extend the `NFZ2` 
        # at level `z.infectee - 1` up to time `z.t`. We also transform `z`
        # to a `NoFlyInfection` when we add it to `processed_infections`, to
        # signal that it should never become infected.
	    NFZ3[z.infectee - 1] = z.t 
	    push!(processed_infections, NoFlyInfection(z))
        # Uncomment for tracking information
        # @info "Conversion of infection into $(NoFlyInfection(z))"
	
	end
    
    # Return the new `CEvolution`: NOTE it is built using a new `Innovation` `iv_mod`!
    iv_mod = Innovation(ev.initial.n, processed_infections, removals, cremovals)
    return CEvolution(ev.initial, iv_mod, LFE=LFE, NFZ1=NFZ1, NFZ2=NFZ2, NFZ3=NFZ3)
end ;
```


Here is step `1` of the evolution of the conditioned epidemic in algorithmic time.
```{julia}
ev2_final  = one_step(ev1, iv2c)
```


Substitution of appropriate inactivated removals
------------------------------------------------
The first step is to create a new `Innovation` which 

(a) removes _all_ old unconditioned
`Removal`s (@fig-test-03-removals1) and 
(b) inserts those new `Removal`s which remain inactivated (@fig-test-03-removals2).
```{julia}
iv2_1 = Innovation(initial.n, ev1.infections, R[], ev1.cremovals)
ev2_1 = CEvolution(initial, iv2_1)
iv2_2 = Innovation(initial.n, ev2_1.infections, 
    EpidemicsCFTP.inactive_removals(ev1, iv2c), ev2_1.cremovals)
ev2_2 = CEvolution(initial, iv2_2)
```

```{julia}
#| echo: false
depict("test-03-removals1", new_figure(
    draw_evolution!(deepcopy(lines_plot), ev2_1, duration, theme=theme, select=MOST),
        title="Old removals removed")
) ;
depict("test-03-removals2", new_figure(
    draw_evolution!(deepcopy(lines_plot), ev2_2, duration, theme=theme, select=MOST),
        title="New inactive removals inserted")
) ;
```


::: {#fig-test-03-removals layout-ncol=2}

![Conditioned evolution `ev2_1`, step 2a.](image/test-03-removals1.pdf){#fig-test-03-removals1}

![Conditioned evolution `ev2_2`, step 2b.](image/test-03-removals2.pdf){#fig-test-03-removals2}

Modifying inactivated removal structure. Step 2a removes _all_ unconditioned old `Removal`s:
step 2b inserts precisely new `Removal`s which would _not_ be activated by the old evolution.

:::


Modifying conditional removal structure
---------------------------------------

The next step is to substitute only those `CRemoval`s which remain activated, while continuing
to use the old `Infection`s
(@fig-test-04-cremovals1 shows relevant `Innovation`, @fig-test-04-cremovals2 shows `CEvolution`).
```{julia}
iv2_3 = Innovation(initial.n, ev2_2.infections, ev2_2.removals, 
    EpidemicsCFTP.resulting_cremovals(ev1, iv2c))
ev2_3 = CEvolution(initial, iv2_3)
```

```{julia}
#| echo: false
depict("test-04-cremovals1", new_figure(
    draw_innovation!(deepcopy(lines_plot), iv2_3, theme=theme, select=ELEMENTS),
        title="Innovation up to new CRemovals")
) ;
depict("test-04-cremovals2", new_figure(
    draw_evolution!(deepcopy(lines_plot), ev2_3, duration, theme=theme, select=MOST),
        title="Resulting evolution")
) ;
```

Notice that the same `CRemoval`s result if we use `ev2_1` or `ev2_2` rather than `ev1`.
```{julia}
@assert EpidemicsCFTP.resulting_cremovals(ev1, iv2c) == EpidemicsCFTP.resulting_cremovals(ev2_1, iv2c)
@assert EpidemicsCFTP.resulting_cremovals(ev1, iv2c) == EpidemicsCFTP.resulting_cremovals(ev2_2, iv2c)
```

::: {#fig-test-04-cremovals layout-ncol=2}

![Innovation with modified removals `iv2_3`.](image/test-04-cremovals1.pdf){#fig-test-04-cremovals1}

![Resulting conditioned evolution `ev2_3`.](image/test-04-cremovals2.pdf){#fig-test-04-cremovals2}

Modifying conditional removal structure. `CRemoval` marks (but not times) altered only when 
they still lead to activation of the relevant `CRemoval`.

:::

{{< pagebreak >}}


Adding infections from the \LFE
-------------------------------
For the present, we compute explicitly with `EpidemicsCFTP.last_feasible_evolution0`.
```{julia}
last_feasible_history        = EpidemicsCFTP.last_feasible_evolution0(duration, ev2_3, iv2c,
                                        conditioned=true)
last_feasible_new_infections = AI[z for z ∈ last_feasible_history ∩ iv2c.infections]
perpetuated_infections       = P[PInfection(z) for z ∈ last_feasible_history ∩ ev2_3.infections]
other_older_infections       = setdiff(ev2_3.infections, 
                                    AI[z for z ∈ last_feasible_history if z isa AI])
iv2_4 = Innovation(initial.n, perpetuated_infections ∪ last_feasible_new_infections ∪ 
                        other_older_infections, ev2_3.removals, ev2_3.cremovals)
ev2_4 = CEvolution(initial, iv2_4, 
    LFE=EpidemicsCFTP.last_feasible_evolution0(duration, ev2_3, iv2c, conditioned=true))
```

```{julia}
#| echo: false
depict("test-05-LFE1", new_figure(
    draw_innovation!(deepcopy(lines_plot), iv2_4, theme=theme, select=ELEMENTS),
        title="Innovation with LFE infections")
) ;
depict("test-05-LFE2", new_figure(
    draw_evolution!(deepcopy(lines_plot), ev2_4, duration, theme=theme, select=MOST | LFE),
        title="Evolution with LFE infections")
) ;
```


::: {#fig-test-05-LFE layout-ncol=2}

![Innovation with LFE infections added (`iv2_4`).](image/test-05-LFE1.pdf){#fig-test-05-LFE1}

![Resulting conditioned evolution `ev2_4`.](image/test-05-LFE2.pdf){#fig-test-05-LFE2}

This adds \LFE (LFE) infections, calculated using `iv2c`, also highlighting
the region lying between the
LFE trajectory and the removal boundary.
Note perpetuation of the activated infection from time line 2 to time line 3,
carried over from `ev2_3`.

:::

Computing the \NOFLYZONE
------------------------
We have already created `ev2_final` to hold the `CEvolution` of the next algorithmic step.

```{julia}
println(sprint(show, MIME("text/plain"), ev2_final.infections))
@assert ev2_final.infections == [I(0.75,1,2), I(0.8,3,4), I(1.5,1,2), XI(1.5,2,3), KI(2.5,1,2), 
                                    P(3.0,2,3), XI(3.3,3,4), I(3.6,4,5), NF(3.9,4,5), 
                                    I(4.4,3,4), KI(4.5,1,3)]
@assert ev2_final.removals   == [R(0.5,2), R(1.2,4), R(2,3), KR(3.3,1), R(4.5,5), KR(4.8,1)]
@assert ev2_final.cremovals  == [C(2,2), C(4,2)]
@assert ev2_final.LFE        == [I(1.5,1,2), C(2,2), I(3,2,3), C(4,2)]
@assert ev2_final.NFZ1       == [-Inf, 0.5, 2.0, 1.2, 4.5]
@assert ev2_final.NFZ2       == [-Inf, 0.5, 2.0, 2.0, 4.5]
@assert ev2_final.NFZ3       == [-Inf, 0.5, 2.0, 3.9, 4.5]
```

Field names of `ev2_final` and a verbose list of contents can be displayed using
```julia
DataFrame(name=[fieldnames(typeof(ev2_final))...], type=[fieldtypes(typeof(ev2_final))...])
dump(ev2_final)
```

Finally, some tests.
```{julia}
max_removal_time = repeat([-Inf], ev2_4.initial.n)
for z ∈ [z for z ∈ ev2_4.removals if z < ev2_4.finis[z.target]]
    max_removal_time[z.target] = max(max_removal_time[z.target], z.t)
end
nofly_envelope = accumulate(max, max_removal_time)
@assert nofly_envelope == ev2_final.NFZ2
```

```{julia}
@assert ev2_2.removals  == ev2_final.removals
@assert ev2_3.cremovals == ev2_4.cremovals == ev2_final.cremovals
```

{{< pagebreak >}}






\appendix

Unit tests
==========
Preliminaries
-------------
The following unit tests should eventually be incorporated in `EpidemicsCFTP/test`
test files. To aid concise expression, 
we define some abbreviations and a function to sort `AbstractIncident`s.
We also add some structures used later for defining and testing
`Innovation`s and `AbstractEvolution`s.
```{julia}
AI = AbstractInfection; I = Infection; P = PInfection; R = Removal; C = CRemoval;
AR = AbstractRemoval;  KR = KilledRemoval;    

infections  = AI[I(2t-1, t, t+1) for t ∈ [1,2]] ∪ AI[I(0,3,4), I(2,4,5)]
uremovals   = R[R(2t, t) for t ∈ [1,2]] ∪ [R(1,5), R(3,5), R(4.9,5)]
removals    = R[R(1,5), R(3,5), R(4.9,5)]
cremovals   = C[C(2t, t) for t ∈ [1,2]] 
trajectory  = SIR[SIR(0,4,1,0), SIR(1,3,2,0), SIR(2,3,1,1), SIR(3,2,2,1), SIR(4,2,1,2)]
uhistory    = [I(1,1,2), R(2,1), I(3,2,3), R(4,2)]
history     = [I(1,1,2), C(2,1), I(3,2,3), C(4,2)]

uiv1  = Innovation(initial.n, infections, uremovals)
uev1  = Evolution(initial, uiv1)
iv1   = Innovation(initial.n, infections, removals, cremovals)
ev1   = CEvolution(initial, iv1)
```

{{< pagebreak >}}

Testing unconditioned and conditioned versions of `AbstractEvolution`
---------------------------------------------------------------------
These tests are intended to check that fields are correctly filled.
```{julia}
begin ;  title = string(Evolution)
    @testset "EpidemicsCFTP: $(rpad(title, 23))" begin
        @test uev1.infections  == sort(infections)
        @test uev1.removals    == sort(uremovals)
        @test uev1.chronology  == sort(infections ∪ uremovals)
        @test uev1.trajectory  == trajectory
        @test uev1.history     == uhistory
    end
end

begin ; title = string(CEvolution)
    @testset "EpidemicsCFTP: $(rpad(title, 23))" begin
        @test sort(uremovals) == [R(z) for z ∈ sort(removals ∪ cremovals)]
        @test ev1.infections   == sort(infections)
        @test ev1.removals     == sort(removals)
        @test ev1.chronology   == sort(infections ∪ removals ∪ cremovals)
        @test ev1.trajectory   == trajectory
        @test ev1.history      == history
    end ;
end ;
```

{{< pagebreak >}}

Substitution of various removals
--------------------------------
The current task is to check removal of all inactive `Removal`s and application of
functions `inactive_removals` and `resulting_cremovals` from `EpidemicsCFTP`.

The first test set considers `ev2_1`, obtained by removing all inactivated `Removal`s.
History and trajectory should not change, while the chronology should be obtained by 
subtracting inactive `Removal`s.
```{julia}
iv2_1   = Innovation(initial.n, infections, R[], cremovals)
ev2_1   = CEvolution(initial, iv2_1)
begin ; title = "Removing Removals"
    @testset "EpidemicsCFTP: $(rpad(title, 23))" begin
        @test ev2_1.trajectory == ev1.trajectory
        @test ev2_1.history    == ev1.history
        @test ev2_1.chronology == setdiff(ev1.chronology, ev1.removals)
    end
end ;
```
Now consider `ev2_2`, obtained by using `EpidemicsCFTP.inactive_removals`
to add in only the inactive removals from the candidate `Innovation` `iv2c` 
(not activated by the trajectory of `ev1` equivalently `ev2_1`).

```{julia}
infections2 = AI[I(2t-1.5, t, t+1) for t ∈ [1,2]] ∪ AI[I(0,3,4), I(2,4,5)]
removals2   = R[R(0.5,5), R(2.5,5), R(2.6,1), R(3.6,1), R(3.9,5), R(4.6,2)]
cremovals2  = C[C(2t, 2t) for t ∈ [1,2]] 

#early_inactivated_removals = [z for z ∈ removals2 if z < uev1.start[z.target]]
#envelope0  = repeat([0.0], initial.n)
#for z ∈ early_inactivated_removals
#    envelope0[z.target]  = max(envelope0[z.target], z.t)
#end
#envelope  = accumulate(max, envelope0)

iv2c  = Innovation(initial.n, infections2, removals2, cremovals2)
iv2_2 = Innovation(initial.n, iv2_1.infections, 
    EpidemicsCFTP.inactive_removals(ev1, iv2c), iv2_1.cremovals)
#ev2_2 = CEvolution(initial, iv2_2, envelope0=envelope0, envelope=envelope)
ev2_2 = CEvolution(initial, iv2_2)
begin ; title = "Inserting Removals"
    early_removals = [z for z ∈ ev2_2.chronology if z isa AR && z < ev2_2.start[z.target]]
    late_removals  = [z for z ∈ ev2_2.chronology if z isa AR && z > ev2_2.finis[z.target]]
    @testset "EpidemicsCFTP: $(rpad(title, 23))" begin
        @test ev2_2.trajectory == ev1.trajectory
        @test [z for z ∈ ev2_2.chronology if z isa R]  == early_removals
        @test [z for z ∈ ev2_2.chronology if z isa KR] == late_removals
    end
end ;
```

Consider the effect of `EpidemicsCFTP.resulting_cremovals`.

```{julia}
iv2_3 = Innovation(initial.n, iv2_2.infections, iv2_2.removals, 
    EpidemicsCFTP.resulting_cremovals(ev2_2, iv2c))
#ev2_3 = CEvolution(initial, iv2_3, envelope0=envelope0, envelope=envelope)
ev2_3 = CEvolution(initial, iv2_3)
begin ; title = "Modifying CRemovals"
    @testset "EpidemicsCFTP: $(rpad(title, 23))" begin
        @test ev2_3.trajectory == ev1.trajectory
        @test ev2_3.infections == ev1.infections
        @test [z for z ∈ ev2_3.chronology if z isa R]  == early_removals
        @test [z for z ∈ ev2_3.chronology if z isa KR] == late_removals
        @test ev2_3.cremovals  == C[C(2,2), C(4,2)] 
    end
end ;
```

Testing the \LFE
----------------

```{julia}
last_feasible_history =
    EpidemicsCFTP.last_feasible_evolution0(duration, ev2_3, iv2c, conditioned=true)
last_feasible_new_infections = AI[z for z ∈ last_feasible_history ∩ iv2c.infections]
perpetuated_infections       = P[PInfection(z) for z ∈ last_feasible_history ∩ ev2_3.infections]
other_older_infections       = setdiff(ev2_3.infections, AI[z for z ∈ last_feasible_history if z isa AI])
iv2_4 = Innovation(initial.n, perpetuated_infections ∪ last_feasible_new_infections ∪
                        other_older_infections, ev2_3.removals, ev2_3.cremovals)
ev2_4 = CEvolution(initial, iv2_4, LFE=last_feasible_history)

begin ; title = "Last feasible evolution"
    LFE_target = [I(1.0,1,2), C(2.0,2), I(3.0,2,3), C(4.0,2)]
    @testset "EpidemicsCFTP: $(rpad(title, 23))" begin
        @test ev2_4.LFE == LFE_target
    end
end ;
```
